title: Property
body_md: \textit{Monotonicity in the level of intransparency.} The sets of feasible policies are nested in $\tau$; that is, $\Pi(\tau_1)\subseteq\Pi(\tau_2)$ for any $\tau_1\leq\tau_2$. Hence, the optimal expected average reward $\bar{R}^{\pi^*}(\tau)$ is nondecreasing in the level of intransparency $\tau$, pointing to an inherent incentive to distort probabilities.

title: Property
body_md: \textit{Uniqueness of fully transparent probability displays under non-anticipatory allocation.} Consider a fixed, fully specified, and non-anticipatory allocation scheme $\alpha$ that uniquely determines the joint allocation outcome for all orders $o\in\mathcal{O}_k^A$ in every pre-decision state $S_k\in\mathcal{S}:t_k\in\mathcal{T}^A$ independent of pending orders $o'\in\mathcal{O}_k:t_{o'}^A>t_k$. Under full transparency ($\tau=0$), $\alpha$ admits exactly one feasible and hence optimal solution for the displayed probabilities, invariant to the underlying reward function.\\[-0.25cm]

title: Property
body_md: \textit{Consider a fixed, fully specified, and non-anticipatory allocation scheme $\alpha$. For every pre-decision state $S_k\in\mathcal{S}:t_k\in\mathcal{T}^A$, the allocation scheme $\alpha$ uniquely determines the joint allocation outcome for all orders $o\in\mathcal{O}_k^A$ independent of pending orders $o'\in\mathcal{O}_k:t_{o'}^A>t_k$. Then, conditional on $\alpha$, the truthful probabilities and thus the probabilities displayed under full transparency $\tau=0$ are unique for every pre-decision state $S\in\mathcal{S}^p$. Therefore, it suffices to identify the single policy feasible under the transparency constraints to find the optimal policy $\pi^*_\alpha$ given $\alpha$.}\\[-0.25cm]

title: Proof
body_md:
For an order $o$ arising at decision epoch $k$, define its time horizon in the system by $h_o=t^A_o-t_k$. Because (i) the points in time $t_k$ are discrete, (ii) $t^A_o$ is finite, and (iii) probability display and allocation occur at distinct decision epochs, it holds that $h_o\in\mathbb{N}$.

For every $h\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{U}(h)$ denote the following statement: \textit{For every probability display pre-decision state $S_k\in\mathcal{S}^p$ and hypothetical order $o_{kj}$ arising if request $r_k$ chooses service option $j\in\mathcal{J}^P$ with $h_{o_{kj}}=h$, the truthful allocation probabilities $\psi^\pi_{o_{kj}}(S_{kj}^c)$ for $o_{kj}$ exist and are uniquely determined. Consequently, under full transparency, the probability-display vector $P^{\pi_\alpha}(S_k)$ exists and is unique.} Note that the allocation time $t_{r_k}^A$ is an attribute of the request such that all service options $j\in\mathcal{J}$ lead to the same horizon $h_{o_{kj}}$. We prove $\mathcal{U}(h)$ for every $h\in\mathbb{N}$ by induction.

For the base case, consider $h=1$, meaning that the hypothetical order $o_{kj}$ arising in $k$ is allocated at the subsequent decision epoch $k+1$. By the prescribed ordering of events, no additional probability display decision occurs between the creation and allocation of $o_{kj}$. Hence, every order that can affect its allocation is already represented in post-choice state $S_{kj}^c$, and the exogenous-information distribution $\mathbb{P}(W_{k+1}^s|S_{kj}^c)$ together with the transition function $S_{k+1}=S^{MW^s}(S_{kj}^c,W^s_{k+1})$ uniquely determine the distribution of the next pre-decision state $S_{k+1}$. Conditional on each realization of the latter, the fully specified allocation scheme $\alpha$ determines a unique joint allocation outcome for all orders $o\in\mathcal{O}_{k+1}^A$, which includes $o_{kj}$. Therefore, the truthful allocation probabilities of $o_{kj}$ for every $j\in\mathcal{J}^P$ exist and are unique. Under full transparency, the displayed probabilities must coincide with the truthful probabilities, establishing $\mathcal{U}(1)$.

For the induction step, fix an arbitrary $h\geq2$ and suppose that $\mathcal{U}(h')$ holds for every $h'<h$. Consider an arbitrary pre-decision state $S_k\in\mathcal{S}^p$ with hypothetical order $o_{kj}$ satisfying $t^A_{o_{kj}}-t_k=h$. Additional requests may arise before $t_{o_{kj}}^A$ and generate orders allocated before or jointly with $o_{kj}$. Consider any such order $o'$ arising at a later decision epoch $k'$ with $t_k<t_{k'}<t^A_{o_{kj}}$. There are two relevant cases to distinguish.

\begin{itemize}
    \item Case 1: $t^A_{o'}\leq t^A_{o_{kj}}$. Because $\alpha$ is non-anticipatory, $o'$ can affect the allocation outcome of $o_{kj}$ only if $t^A_{o'}\leq t^A_{o_{kj}}$. Its horizon $h_{o'}$ satisfies
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
    h_{o'} =
    t^A_{o'}-t_{k'}\leq t^A_{o_{kj}}-t_{k'}< t^A_{o_{kj}}-t_k=h
    \end{aligned}
    \]
    Since probability display and allocation occur at distinct decision epochs, $1\leq h_{o'}<h$. Hence, every future order capable of affecting the allocation of $o_{kj}$ has a horizon in $\{1,\ldots,h-1\}$ and is covered by the induction hypothesis. The truthful allocation probabilities, and therefore the fully transparent display vector at epoch $k'$, are thus uniquely determined. Since the customer-choice model $\mathbb{P}(W_{k'+1}^c|S_{k'},P^{\pi_\alpha}(S_{k'}))$ uniquely maps the state and probability display vector into a choice probability distribution, the conditional distribution of the customer's choice is unique.
    \item Case 2: $t^A_{o'}> t^A_{o_{kj}}$. The order $o'$ is allocated strictly after order $o_{kj}$. Following its creation, $o'$ is included in the updated set of pending orders $O_{k'+1}$, but it does not occupy capacity before its allocation. Moreover, by non-anticipativity of $\alpha$, neither the existence nor the characteristics of $o'$ affect any allocation decision made at or before $t^A_{o_{kj}}$. Additionally, the presence of $o'$ does not influence the conditional distribution of the exogenous information relevant to the allocation of $o_{kj}$, including capacity availability, request arrivals, and customer choices that may affect allocations up to $t^A_{o_{kj}}$. Consequently, conditional on any realization of the process up to $t^A_{o_{kj}}$, the allocation outcome of $o_{kj}$ is invariant to $o'$. Hence, when constructing the conditional distribution of the allocation state for $o_{kj}$, the customer choice and subsequent state information associated exclusively with $o'$ can be marginalized out. Orders allocated strictly after $o_{kj}$ therefore do not affect the truthful allocation probability of $o_{kj}$.
\end{itemize}

The finite composition of state transitions, which follow unique conditional distributions, together uniquely determines the probability distribution of the allocation state for order $o_{kj}$ and the associated set of orders to be allocated. Conditional on each realization, scheme $\alpha$ uniquely determines the joint allocation outcome or its probability distribution. Hence, the truthful allocation probability $\psi_{o_{kj}}^{\pi_\alpha}(S_{kj}^c)$ exists and has a unique value. Therefore, the probability display vector in pre-decision state $S_k$ is unique, and $\mathcal{U}(h)$ holds.

By induction, $\mathcal{U}(h)$ holds for every $h\in\mathbb{N}$. Since $S_k$ and $j$ were arbitrary, the truthful allocation probabilities exist and are uniquely determined in every post-choice state. Consequently, under $\tau=0$, the probability display decision is unique in every pre-decision state. Therefore, the full-transparency constraints admit a unique policy conditional on $\alpha$, which is the optimal policy $\pi_\alpha^*$ given $\alpha$.
